content.text:
Here is what the official Cursor docs say about **Max Mode**.

## 1. What Max Mode is

Max Mode is a **legacy-plan feature that extends a model's context window** past Cursor's default cap. It is **not** a separate chat mode like Agent, Ask, Plan, or Debug.

From [Max Mode on legacy plans](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/max-mode):

> Max Mode is available only on legacy request-based plans. It extends a model's context window beyond the default limit.

The models/pricing docs say the same thing, plus billing:

> Max Mode is available only on legacy request-based plans. It extends a model's context window beyond the default limit and is billed at the model's API rate plus 20%.

On **current usage-based plans** (Pro, Pro Plus, Ultra, etc.), Max Mode does not exist. From [Usage and limits](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/usage-limits):

> Current usage-based plans don't include Max Mode.

Those plans already bill by tokens, so you pick a model (and any extended context the model supports) without a Max toggle.

## 2. What it changes

| Area | What the docs say |
| --- | --- |
| **Context window** | Extends the window **beyond the default limit**. Some models support **up to 1M tokens** of extended context. |
| **Models** | Some models **require** Max Mode on legacy request-based plans. Selecting them turns Max on automatically. |
| **Pricing** | **API rate + 20%**. A larger window can also use **more tokens per request**. |
| **Tools** | Not documented as changing. Agent still has the same tools (search, edit, terminal, browser, etc.). |
| **Intelligence / reasoning** | Current docs do **not** say Max Mode makes the model smarter. Older forum threads claimed extra reasoning or larger file reads; that is **not** in today's official pages. |
| **Agent vs Max** | Different layers. **Agent** is the assistant that edits files and runs tools. **Max Mode** is a model-selector toggle that only affects context size and billing on legacy plans. |

### Models that require Max Mode on legacy plans

From [Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing):

**Anthropic**
- Claude 4.5 Opus, Claude 4.5 Sonnet
- Claude 4.6 Opus, Claude 4.6 Sonnet
- Claude 4.7 Opus
- Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1
- Claude Opus 4.7 (fast mode)
- Claude Opus 4.8 (including fast mode)
- Claude Opus 5 (including fast mode)
- Claude Sonnet 5

**OpenAI**
- GPT-5.3 Codex
- GPT-5.4 (long context up to 1M, **2x input pricing**)
- GPT-5.5 (long context up to 1M, **2x input pricing**)
- GPT-5.6 Sol (long context up to 1M, **2x input pricing**)

**Moonshot**
- Kimi K3 (up to 1M, no long-context surcharge)

Several Claude models (4.5/4.6/4.7 Sonnet and Opus, Opus 4.8/5, Sonnet 5) and Kimi K3 document **up to 1M tokens** with **no extra long-context surcharge**. GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.6 Sol also support **up to 1M**, but with **2x input pricing** for long context.

The docs do **not** publish a single default-vs-Max token number for every model. They only say Max Mode lifts Cursor's default working window, and they list 1M where a model supports extended context.

Cursor-native models (Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5, Composer 2.5) are **not** listed as requiring Max Mode.

## 3. When to use it vs when not to

**Use it** (legacy request-based plans only) when the task actually needs more than the default window: large multi-file work, long sessions, or a model that only runs with Max enabled.

From the Max Mode help page:

> Use Max Mode when a task needs more context than the model's default window. The default context window works well for most coding tasks.

**Skip it** when:
- You are on a **current usage-based plan** (no Max Mode; just pick the model).
- Everyday coding fits the default window.
- You want **predictable per-request** billing on a legacy plan. Max Mode switches those requests to token billing + 20%.

## 4. How to enable it

From [Max Mode on legacy plans](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/max-mode):

1. Confirm you are on a **legacy request-based plan**.
2. Open the **model selector** in chat or Agent.
3. **Toggle Max Mode on**. It stays on across conversations.
4. Models that require Max Mode **enable it automatically** when you select them.

If you do not see a Max toggle, that matches current docs: usage-based plans do not include Max Mode.

CLI docs do not document a `--max` flag. Max Mode is described as an editor model-selector setting.

## 5. Caveats

- **Legacy only.** Current usage-based plans do not have it.
- **Costs more.** API rate **plus 20%**, and a bigger window can send more tokens.
- **Some models force it** on legacy plans (Opus 5, Fable, GPT-5.6 Sol, and others listed above).
- **Long-context pricing still varies.** Claude extended context is often same per-token rates; GPT-5.4 / 5.5 / 5.6 Sol long context is **2x input**.
- **Claude 4 Sonnet 1M** is called out as potentially very expensive: **2x cost when input exceeds 200k tokens**.
- Docs do **not** claim Max Mode is slower, smarter, or gives extra tools. The documented change is **more context**, at **higher token cost**.

**Sources:** [Max Mode on legacy plans](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/max-mode), [Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing), [Usage and limits](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/usage-limits), [Agent mode](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/agent).
